chunks.text: 28-year-old female, Senior Official or Manager, resident of Ang Mo Kio, Singapore.
General Anesthesia with Single-shot Ultrasound-Guided Transversus Abdominis Plane (TAP) Block for Postoperative Pain Management

segments.speaker: PROVIDER
segments.text: Good morning, Mr./Ms./Mrs. [Patient's Name]. I'm [Provider's Name], the anesthesiologist who will be taking care of you during your surgery today. I'd like to go through a few important questions to ensure your safety and comfort during the procedure. Is that okay with you?

segments.speaker: PATIENT
segments.text: Yes, of course. I'm ready.

segments.speaker: PROVIDER
segments.text: Thank you. Let's start with your medical history. Can you briefly tell me about the reason for your surgery today?

segments.speaker: PATIENT
segments.text: Sure. I've been having a lot of pain in my abdomen, especially after eating. The doctor found stones in my gallbladder, so they're removing it laparoscopically.

segments.speaker: PROVIDER
segments.text: Understood. Now, regarding your medications, I see from your records that you're on Metformin, Gliclazide, Atorvastatin, and you've stopped Ranitidine. Can you please confirm if there have been any changes to your medication list since your last review?

segments.speaker: PATIENT
segments.text: Actually, yes. I stopped taking Gliclazide a few months ago because I was having too many low sugar episodes. My doctor switched me to Sitagliptin 100mg once daily instead.

segments.speaker: PROVIDER
segments.text: Thank you for letting me know. It's important we have the most up-to-date information. Have you experienced any new allergic reactions to medications recently?

segments.speaker: PATIENT
segments.text: Oh, yes. I had an allergic reaction to Ceftriaxone last year. I got hives all over my body, so I shouldn't have that antibiotic again.

segments.speaker: PROVIDER
segments.text: Thank you for sharing that. We'll make sure to note that in your chart. Your allergies were previously listed as only Penicillin with a rash. This is an important update.

segments.speaker: PATIENT
segments.text: Yes, I should have mentioned it earlier, but it slipped my mind.

segments.speaker: PROVIDER
segments.text: No worries at all. That's why we do this interview — to catch any updates. Now, regarding your diabetes, how well-controlled is it on your current medications?

segments.speaker: PATIENT
segments.text: It's been pretty good since I switched to Sitagliptin. My fasting sugar is usually around 120-140, and I don't have as many spikes as before.

segments.speaker: PROVIDER
segments.text: Excellent. And how about your weight and mobility? You're listed as having a BMI of 32. How do you feel about your overall fitness level?

segments.speaker: PATIENT
segments.text: I know I'm overweight, but I can still walk and do daily activities without too much trouble. I just get tired faster than before.

segments.speaker: PROVIDER
segments.text: That's helpful to know. Have you had any previous surgeries or anesthesia before?

segments.speaker: PATIENT
segments.text: No, this is my first time. I'm a bit nervous, but I trust the team.

segments.speaker: PROVIDER
segments.text: That's completely normal. We're here to make sure everything goes smoothly. Finally, have you had anything to eat or drink since midnight?

segments.speaker: PATIENT
segments.text: No, I've been fasting as instructed. Just a sip of water with my morning meds, but that was hours ago.

segments.speaker: PROVIDER
segments.text: Perfect. Thank you so much for going through all that with me. I'll be using general anesthesia for your surgery, and we'll also be doing a Transversus Abdominis Plane block under ultrasound guidance to help with your pain after surgery. Any questions for me before we proceed?

segments.speaker: PATIENT
segments.text: No, I think that's all. Thank you for explaining everything so clearly.

segments.speaker: PROVIDER
segments.text: [08:00] induction propofol one hundred twenty milligrams

segments.speaker: PROVIDER
segments.text: [08:02] tube in, grade one view

segments.speaker: PROVIDER
segments.text: [08:05] initiating ultrasound-guided TAP block with bupivacaine twenty-five milligrams

segments.speaker: PROVIDER
segments.text: [08:10] two liters of lactated ringers administered

segments.speaker: PROVIDER
segments.text: [08:20] mean arterial pressure dropped to fifty-five, atropine one milligram given

segments.speaker: PROVIDER
segments.text: [08:40] surgery completion, reversal with neostigmine two milligrams and sugammadex sixteen milligrams

segments.speaker: PROVIDER
segments.text: Hi there, how are you feeling now after the surgery?

segments.speaker: PATIENT
segments.text: I'm okay, I guess. Still a bit groggy, but I can talk.

segments.speaker: PROVIDER
segments.text: That's expected. On a scale from 0 to 10, how would you rate your pain right now?

segments.speaker: PATIENT
segments.text: Maybe a 3 or 4. There's some discomfort, but it's manageable.

segments.speaker: PROVIDER
segments.text: Good. Have you felt nauseous at all since waking up?

segments.speaker: PATIENT
segments.text: No, not really. My stomach feels fine so far.

segments.speaker: PROVIDER
segments.text: Excellent. How's your breathing? Any tightness or difficulty catching your breath?

segments.speaker: PATIENT
segments.text: No, I'm breathing fine. Just a bit tired from the anesthesia, I think.

segments.speaker: PROVIDER
segments.text: Understood. Do you remember anything from the operating room today?

segments.speaker: PATIENT
segments.text: Not really. I remember going in and then waking up here. So I guess I was out completely.

segments.speaker: PROVIDER
segments.text: That's normal with general anesthesia. Given your diabetes and weight, we'll keep a close eye on your sugar levels and mobility post-op. Any concerns or questions from your side?

segments.speaker: PATIENT
segments.text: No, I think that's all. I just want to go home soon and rest.

Patient reported stopping Gliclazide due to frequent low sugar episodes and switched to Sitagliptin 100mg once daily.
Patient has a history of resolved pneumonia (5 years ago), fully healed fractured wrist at age 12, and mild depression not on medications.
Patient has allergies to Penicillin (rash) and Ceftriaxone (hives).
Scheduled procedure is Laparoscopic Cholecystectomy under General Anesthesia with Single-shot Ultrasound-Guided Transversus Abdominis Plane (TAP) Block for Postoperative Pain Management.

Surgery completed with reversal using Neostigmine 2mg and Sugammadex 16mg.
Postoperatively, patient reports pain level of 3-4 on a scale of 0-10, describing it as manageable discomfort.
Patient denies postoperative nausea or vomiting (PONV) and reports feeling fine in terms of stomach comfort.
Patient's breathing is unremarkable with no reported tightness or difficulty catching breath.
Patient has no recall of the operating room, consistent with general anesthesia.
Patient is alert and able to communicate postoperatively, though still feeling somewhat groggy from anesthesia.
